questions.question: What corpus invariants does Taxonomy.validate enforce before matching prompts?
options: Only that every prompt has the same length
Only that fixture severity is an integer
Nonempty prompts, unique IDs, known categories, severity 1–5, and at least seven fixtures per category
Exactly one fixture per category and no duplicate subtypes
questions.explanation: validate checks all of those corpus properties. The default corpus has 50 fixtures across six categories; it is not restricted to one fixture or one subtype per category.

questions.question: What normalization does _trigrams apply before counting character trigrams?
options: It removes all vowels and preserves case
It tokenizes on punctuation and sorts words
It hashes each full word and ignores whitespace
It strips outer whitespace, lowercases, and collapses whitespace runs to one space
questions.explanation: _trigrams uses re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text.strip().lower()). It then counts each overlapping three-character window of the cleaned string.

questions.question: How does Taxonomy.match choose a fixture for a new prompt?
options: It returns the fixture with the highest trigram cosine score, even without a threshold fallback
It rejects the prompt whenever its score is below 0.5
It samples a category from the severity histogram
It requires an exact prompt string match
questions.explanation: The matcher computes cosine similarity against every stored fixture and retains the maximum. Even a low-scoring prompt receives the best available MatchResult; there is no unknown category threshold.

questions.question: Which severity and identifier properties must every default Fixture satisfy?
options: Severity 0–1 and an ID that may repeat within a category
Severity 1–5 inclusive and a globally unique nonempty ID
Severity 1–100 and an ID derived from the prompt hash
Severity must equal the category's fixture count
questions.explanation: validate enforces the inclusive SEVERITY_RANGE (1, 5) and rejects duplicate IDs. Fixture IDs are separate from categories and need not encode severity.

questions.question: What is the shape of score_matrix for three prompts and the default 50-fixture corpus?
options: (50, 3), because fixtures are rows
(3,), one best score per prompt
(3, 50), one cosine score for each prompt-fixture pair
(6, 50), one row per taxonomy category
questions.explanation: score_matrix appends one row per prompt and one column per stored fixture, so three prompts produce a NumPy array with shape (3, 50).

questions.question: Which top-level fields does Taxonomy.serialize write for the downstream artifact?
options: Only the best match and its cosine score
A raw NumPy matrix and the Python class name
The six category names and a list of prompts without severities
version "1.0", categories, serialized fixtures, and aggregate stats
questions.explanation: serialize returns the stable artifact envelope: version 1.0, the category list, every Fixture converted with asdict, and stats including counts and severity histogram.
